decision: rejected: no nonzero pitch padding improves both retained and zero-padding controls
scope: Isolated banks of 28 distinct weights for each retained encoder projection family. Seeded BF16 inputs; no full-request latency claim.
arithmetic: Cloned retained kernels change only weight row addressing. TMA changes descriptor leading stride. Tile geometry, K-loop order, BF16 roundings, GEGLU corrections and split-K reduction are unchanged. MLPWo returns retained BF16 partials for the first 27 layers and reduces the last layer.
allocation: All added storage zero initialized and original BF16 values verified bitwise. All paddings preserve 16-byte TMA stride alignment.
control_note: Zero-padding clones differ from original timing by less than 1%, showing that copying/reinstantiating alone can change results. No nonzero padding clearly exceeds both controls.
stop_reason: The isolated bank did not establish a candidate, so real-activation and full-request gates were not run.
timing_method: Exclusive experiment lock; separate CUDA graphs per variant, randomized variant order for 9 rounds, 50 replays per sample. Unused row-padding storage initialized to zero.
